title: Third-party subprocessor mapping and region-pin implications
content:
Purpose
This note captures an initial mapping of third-party subprocessors (cloud, storage, network, managed services) and how region pinning decisions affect contractual obligations, telemetry collection, operator actions, and enforcement surface area. It is a working doc for eng-private-deployments + legal + security to iterate on before we fold into the residency playbook.

Scope and definitions
- Subprocessor: any downstream vendor or managed service that touches tenant data in a way relevant to residency (storage, compute, backups, monitoring agents, logs exports, CDNs).
- Region pin (hard pin): tenant data and inference requests must remain within a specific sovereign region and cannot transit external regions except allowed exceptions.
- Soft pin / affinity: best-effort regional preference; fallbacks permitted for availability.

Top-level risks introduced by pinning for subprocessors
1) Hidden data paths: agents, sidecars, or vendor telemetry might create egress channels (metrics, crash dumps, heartbeats).
2) Backup & DR locations: vendor snapshot/backup policies may replicate to central storage outside pinned region.
3) Support workflows: vendor support tooling often requires cross-region access to investigate incidents.
4) SLA mismatch: subprocessors may not provide region-specific SLAs which breaks contractual guarantees.
5) Contractual chain: customers require proof (audit trail) that subprocessors are constrained to region — requires contractual amendments and evidence.

Working inventory (partial)
- Object storage (S3-compatible): used for model artifacts, customer uploads. Pin implication: must choose region-specific buckets, disable cross-region replication. Ops action: create bucket naming convention tenant-region-<id>-artifacts, enforce lifecycle and retention tags.
- Block storage / PVs: used on dedicated nodes. Pin implication: ensure PVs created in tenant's AZs; snapshot retention must be region-only. Ops action: modify CSI driver to annotate snapshots with region-pin tag; block cross-account backup jobs.
- Metrics & tracing vendors (hosted): vendor agents often export traces to a central EU/US endpoint. Pin implication: forbidden for hard-pinned customers. Ops action: maintain local telemetry collectors and push anonymized rollups to central systems; add feature flag to disable remote exporters per-tenant.
- Log aggregation services: vendor-managed ingestion may buffer in another region. Pin implication: must use region-local collectors; long-term archive needs region-residency assurance.
- CDNs / edge caching: acceptable for latency; must ensure cached user data TTLs and eviction for pinned tenants; audit caching endpoints.
- Managed DB / caching (Redis as a service): ensure service plan supports regional tenancy and does not failover to control plane in another region.

Telemetry and evidence requirements (what compliance/auditors will ask)
- Proof of data flows: sequence diagrams and sampled flow logs showing ingress -> compute -> storage remain in region.
- Subprocessor contracts: POAAs/DPAs explicitly listing allowed subprocessors and region constraints.
- Audit logs: time-stamped evidence that no egress occurred (network flow logs, S3 access logs, snapshot creation events).
- Operator check-ins: runbooks and a check-list that on tenant onboarding verify each subprocessor mapping is compliant.

Operational checklist for onboarding a pinned tenant (draft)
1) Inventory: generate automated list of used subprocessors for the tenant (model store, metrics, backups, infra-as-a-service).
2) Capability check: for each subprocessor, classify: region-aware (supports region-only), region-conditional (needs config), non-compliant (requires replacement).
3) Config actions: apply region-only configs (bucket flags, exporter disables, backup targets).
4) Contract/legal: kick DPA amendment with subprocessor if non-compliant. Attach evidence to tenant onboarding folder.
5) Telemetry baseline: enable verbose audit logs for first 30 days; schedule daily digest to residency-audit mailbox.
6) Operator signoff: SRE or residency oncall signs off checklist.

Enforcement mechanics (operator & runtime)
- Runtime guards: token-inspecting router tags tenant requests with pin metadata. If a runtime component would dispatch work to a non-local subprocessor (eg model fetch from cross-region), runtime rejects and returns structured error with remediation instructions.
- Observable signals: emit a "subprocessor-pin-violation" metric and attach evidence (request id, candidate target region, component).
- Automated remediation: for non-critical violations (metrics exporters), flip to local collector automatically and create a change-event. For critical violations (backup snapshot to external region), halt the snapshot and escalate to oncall.
- Incident taxonomy: map types to severity and response timeline (e.g., bypassed exporter = Sev3, cross-region snapshot attempt = Sev1).

Contract & legal considerations (notes for legal)
- Add explicit subprocessor list in customer DPAs with placeholder for vendor-specific region support evidence.
- Require subprocessors to provide region-specific SOC/ISO artifacts or signed attestations for region residency controls when used by pinned tenants.
- Define permitted exception flows and an approval workflow (LOB/Legal/Security) with time-boxed mitigations.

Migration and remediation patterns for non-compliant subprocessors
- Replace: run vendor evaluation and migrate to region-compliant vendor (preferred long-term).
- Isolate: introduce a proxy or local adapter that prevents outbound egress from the pinned region while using the existing vendor.
- Contractual workaround: short-term waiver for a specific tenant with enhanced monitoring and indemnification.

Short-term engineering tasks (next 30 days)
- [ ] Add per-tenant telemetry toggle to disable remote exporters (owner: Liam Chen, ENGPD-XX).
- [ ] Inventory job that maps tenant to subprocessors and outputs CSV for legal review (owner: Nora Patel).
- [ ] Draft standard DPA amendment language for subprocessor region restriction (owner: Samir Gupta + legal).
- [ ] Simulator: synthetic test that attempts to trigger known subprocessor egress patterns and asserts runtime guards (owner: Elena Rios).

Open questions / discussion points
- Do we allow read-only cross-region model artifact fetch for non-PI workloads under soft pin? (pros: availability; cons: compliance complexity)
- What is the tolerance for transient telemetry sampling outside region if it's anonymized? Need legal stance.
- How do we present evidence to customers during audits without leaking platform internals? (suggestion: pre-bundled audit packet per tenant).

Appendix A: sample operator remediation script (pseudo)
- detect event: subprocessor-pin-violation triggered -> gather flow logs for request_id -> check if violation was caused by config drift -> if config drift, rollback to last known-good template -> if vendor limitation, create escalation with legal and tag customer folder.

Appendix B: sample onboarding checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Subprocessor inventory CSV attached
- [ ] Bucket replication disabled
- [ ] Telemetry exporters flagged local-only
- [ ] Backup snapshot targets region-only
- [ ] Operator signoff (name/date)

Next steps
- Review with Legal + Security next week (calendar invite sent).
- Convert this doc into a concise section in the residency playbook and a machine-checklist for the onboarding pipeline.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally operational and contains TODOs. Please comment inline in Drive. If you have vendor-specific knowledge (e.g., Splunk agent options, Datadog EU-only endpoints), add a line in the inventory section so we can classify quickly.
